(MarijuanaNews note: Marijuana prohibition offers us some interesting insights into human nature. On the whole, the California Medical Association has a very decent position on medical marijuana. However, it is clear that this was not easy for them. The letter below would be comical if the subject were not so serious.

The Hawaiian Medical Association – on the other hand -- has been fundamentally dishonest in its opposition to the state’s new medical marijuana bill, as was the Maine Medical Association, and others.

Author: Jack C. Lewin, Executive Vice President & CEO, California Medical Association and Former Director of Hawaii Department of Health

MEDICAL MARIJUANA STAND CLARIFIED

Writing in Island Voices, May 9, Pamela Lichty stated that numerous medical organizations, including the California Medical Association (CMA), have " supported the use of medical marijuana. " The article was critical of the Hawaii Medical Association's position on the recent legislation that authorizes, under state law, the use of marijuana for medical purposes.

Lichty supported her statement concerning CMA's policy by quoting a recent amicus curiae (friend of the court) brief filed by CMA in the federal civil litigation brought by the Department of Justice against several California cannabis buyers' clubs.

I would like to clarify CMA's position on the subject: Contrary to Lichty's contention, CMA neither supports nor opposes the medical use of marijuana.
(MarijuanaNews note: Many years ago, the multi-talented Peter Ustinov did a routine in which he played the UN ambassadors from various countries, making noises that sounded like their languages. However, when he played the UK ambassador, he said in his beautiful English: " Her Majesty’s government neither votes Aye, nor does it vote Nay, but under no circumstances should this be construed as an abstention. " He is much funnier than the CMA.)

Rather, CMA has consistently maintained its position that marijuana should be widely available for therapeutic use only if there have been properly controlled clinical studies proving that it is efficacious.

CMA has called upon the federal government to facilitate the availability of high-quality inhaled marijuana and to take other necessary steps to promote such research. CMA supports the removal of marijuana from Schedule I in order to allow greater access for research as well as efforts to obtain federal approval for limited prescriptive access and for an appropriately regulated distribution system.

See
California Medical Association To Support Rescheduling Of Marijuana;
Otherwise Little Accomplished At Summit
and
Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be " Down-Scheduled, "
Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site.
Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?

However, we continue to believe the requirements of the state and federal drug laws serve a critically important function in protecting patients from potentially inefficacious and even dangerous drugs. Hence, CMA does not support the use of the legislative or initiative process to make any unproven and insufficiently tested medicine available to the public. For those reasons, CMA opposed Proposition 215 when it was before the electorate in California.

Thebrief from which Lichty quoted was filed, not specifically to support the medical use of marijuana, but to support the concept of " medical necessity " recently articulated in that litigation by the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals.
See
Major Victory For Medical Marijuana: 9th Circuit Ruling Allows Patients
To Argue Before U.S. District Judge That Their Medical Marijuana Use Is A Fundamental Right.
and links

In the brief, CMA argued that when a patient has tried all available standard therapies without success, that patient with the support and approval of his or her physician should be free to explore other, less conventional treatments.

Such desperate patients, their physicians and others who attempt to aid them should be neither punished nor unnecessarily impeded by governmental enforcement agencies. CMA supported the right of a patient and physician to use any potentially therapeutic modality that may assuage the suffering of a patient who can find relief in no other way.
(MarijuanaNews note: However, under no circumstances should this be construed as actually advocating the medical use of marijuana.)
